newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes lower on NYMEX, Line 63 diffs.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes lower on NYMEX, Line 63 diffs.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices slid in reaction to sharply lower futures and a fall in Line 63 crude differentials, traders said.

NYMEX October crude settled $1.32 a barrel at $23.19, on a late Monday report -- denied by U.S. and Persian Gulf sources -- that the U.S. asked Saudi Arabia to increase crude oil production as compensation for lost Iraqi exports.
Discounts for Line 63 widened by about 50 cents to $3.20/3.00 a barrel under West Texas Intermediate following a purported deal late last week.
Traders said the 30,000-barrel deal consisted of "loss allowance" crude, accumulated portions of oil which pipelines acquire from shippers and resell.
Prenominations for Line 63 are due to start mid-week and outright values were $20.05/20.25, $1 below notional early levels.
California heavy grades were flat late after rising last Thursday on increased posted prices.
Discounts for Kern River were 50/25 cents under postings, with supplies seen tightening as refineries ran more of it.
Greater consumption of heavies came after recent increases in posted prices left light grades at high premiums to heavies, making them less lucrative to process.
Kern River values ranged $15.60/15.90 a barrel, compared to light grade levels in the low $20s.
Outright values for Alaska North Slope crude fell about 40 cents to $20.85/21.15 a barrel.
Differentials for ANS were unchanged from last week's deal at $2.30 a barrel under WTI.
The Trans-Alaska pipeline resumed carrying its normal levels of Alaskan crude over the weekend, after seeing a 30 percent cut late last week, a pipeline spokeswoman said.
